clue.text: Couple under a hundred above sum total

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under the others comes after them in the answer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
on, as in 'on top of', means above
taken as written
to mate is to couple or pair up

explanation.surface: Instructions for a calculation: pair something up beneath a hundred, above a sum, to reach a total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' tells you MATE (Couple) is written below C, ON and SUM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means complete or utter, so a total disaster is a consummate one.

clue.text: Crafty scheme has to accommodate biblical character

parts.note: to put someone up is to give them a bed for the night
Job is the much-tried figure of the Old Testament book

explanation.surface: A sly plan that involves housing a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a rigged arrangement, a deceitful scheme set up in advance.

clue.text: More offensive soldier?

definitions.meaning: comparative of rank in its sense of foul-smelling or gross
a soldier who serves, or has risen from, the ranks

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means rancid or gross, so more rank is more offensive; a ranker is an enlisted soldier.

clue.text: Good representative, a solicitor

parts.note: pi is short for pious, hence good
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: Praising a worthy delegate who happens to be a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it means someone who solicits for prostitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimp solicits custom on behalf of prostitutes, so is literally one who solicits.

clue.text: Incentive which binds Brahminical Cockneys?

indicators.note: Londoners of the East End traditionally drop the initial H of words

parts.note: Brahmins are the priestly caste of Hindus, so Brahminical suggests Hindu
cement is the substance that binds bricks together

explanation.surface: A question about what motivates Brahmins living in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockneys' drops the H from HINDU, giving the dialect form 'INDU, which runs into CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inducement is something offered to persuade, a direct synonym of incentive.

clue.text: Clue about bank coming up, hard, which proves bloomer

indicators.note: the hint wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a hint is a clue

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cay is a low sandbank or reef
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hint about a sandbank, hard going, that turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses the bank in this down clue, and 'about' wraps it in the clue; 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and the hyacinth is a spring bulb grown for its blooms.

clue.text: Land on one's head?

definitions.meaning: a lightweight straw hat worn on the head

explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a Central American nation and also the name of a woven straw hat.

clue.text: Heads raised in shock

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: People's heads lifted in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to shock or stupefy someone.

clue.text: I appreciate that, darling, nothing turns one on — it happens once a month!

indicators.note: the first three pieces together are turned around

parts.note: ta is informal British thanks
luv is a colloquial term of endearment
O looks like zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover thanks a partner, saying nothing arouses them more, with a monthly twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the first three pieces together, so thanks, darling and nothing read as OVULAT; 'turns one on' pretends to be about arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation, the release of an egg, occurs roughly once in each monthly cycle.

clue.text: Such will raise unknown point

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Something will raise an unknown point in a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the leavening agent that makes dough rise, so it is such a thing that raises.

clue.text: Bill may be so conceited

definitions.meaning: a bill, meaning a poster, may be fixed up on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A poster may be stuck up on a wall, and a stuck-up person is conceited.

clue.text: Short bloke in loveless marriage, free

indicators.note: the shortened bloke goes inside the other piece
love is O in tennis scores, so loveless removes an O

parts.note: a union is a marriage

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: chap is British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A man trapped in a passionless marriage breaks free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' uses tennis's love = O, removed from the marriage to give UNIN; 'Short' docks the bloke's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain someone is to free them from restraint.

clue.text: Sticky situation backing non-extremist Tory PM

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a jam is a tight spot

indicators.note: drop the extreme, outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A moderate Conservative prime minister supported through a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns JAM into MAJ; 'non-extremist' strips the outer letters of Tory to leave OR. John Major was a Conservative British prime minister in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major served as British Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997.

clue.text: Good to get together again with fruity thing

parts.note: to re-engage is to engage or join up once more

explanation.surface: Advice to reunite over something fruity.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a green variety of plum, a fruit.

clue.text: Grannies will go berserk with doctor passing round biscuit

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go around the scrambled ones

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner

indicators.note: the grannies' letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Elderly women run riot with their family doctor over a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will go berserk' rearranges the grannies into INGERSNA, and 'passing round' puts the doctor's two letters on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp ginger-flavoured biscuit.

clue.text: Coarse quality needs attention (she isn't refined)

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: refined suggests reprocessing, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A remark that a woman lacking refinement needs attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges SHE ISNT to THINESS; it looks like a description of the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthiness is a robust, unrefined crudeness, a coarse quality.

clue.text: Such a lunatic about to pop through warning signal, one hoping to profit from accident

definitions.text: one hoping to profit from accident

indicators.note: the long middle piece runs through the warning light

parts.note: amber is the warning light on a traffic signal

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the next piece
lunatic means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to lance a boil is to pop it

explanation.surface: A madman about to burst through a traffic light, chasing profit from a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' scrambles SUCH A into U plus CHAS, which wrap the popping word ('about'); all of that goes inside the traffic warning light ('through').
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance chaser is a lawyer who seeks clients among accident victims to win compensation.

clue.text: When terribly lost, read navigation guide

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: When hopelessly lost, consult your guide to navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar is a star used to steer by, notably the Pole Star, hence a navigation guide.

clue.text: The way to overcome beginner in game not quite finished is to battle

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome is to sit on top of the following piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the learner goes inside the trimmed game
the game loses its final letter

parts.note: rugger is British slang for rugby union
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: Advice that the route past a novice in an unfinished match is to fight it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite finished' gives RUGGE, which takes the learner inside; in this down clue the way sits above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to fight or contend, so it can replace battle as a verb.

clue.text: Old writer about to end tale at first profitable

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: the writer goes around the next piece

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to die is to come to an end

indicators.note: take only the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A former author nearly finished with a story that pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives PEDIEN, the writer wrapping the dying, between the former prefix and the tale's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expedient is advantageous or convenient, hence profitable in the broad sense.

clue.text: Cannon for Englishmen abroad?

definitions.meaning: Pom is Australian slang for an English person, so two of them

explanation.definitionFit: The pom-pom was a quick-firing gun; Poms is Australian slang for English people.

clue.text: Where bird found fish

definitions.meaning: a resting place for a bird, a bar or branch

explanation.definitionFit: A perch is a bird's roost and also a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Quick to help out

definitions.meaning: to give an actor a forgotten line

explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means quick or punctual, and to prompt is to help an actor out with a line.

clue.text: Release of man reflected one's fate

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so read backwards

parts.note: semen is what a man releases
I for one plus S, the contraction of is

explanation.surface: A man's discharge, mirrored, shows the destiny awaiting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns SEMEN to NEMES; one's is I'S, giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis means an inescapable downfall or retribution, one's doom or fate.

clue.text: Sea-blue, describing church body might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals the word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: an adjective formed from nave, the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A shade of blue describing a church interior, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The nave is the central body of a church; a made-up adjective 'nave-y' sounds like the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is a dark blue, named after naval uniforms, so it is a blue of the sea.

clue.text: Old dictator grabbing butt of biggest weapon

indicators.note: the dictator takes hold of the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military ruler of old Japan

indicators.note: butt means the end, so take the last letter

explanation.surface: A former tyrant seizing the stock of the largest firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt of biggest' gives T, which goes inside SHOGUN; 'butt' looks like part of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm, a weapon.

clue.text: One's bound to be somewhat user-friendly

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone tied to being fairly easy to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'user-friendly', ignoring the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land of the lord.

clue.text: Character in "Twelfth Night" played?

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Shakespeare's comedy who disguises herself as Cesario
an instrument one plays, larger than a violin

explanation.definitionFit: Viola is Shakespeare's shipwrecked heroine and also a stringed instrument that is played.

clue.text: It's gathered storage tower reversing onto a fortification

indicators.note: the other pieces are added onto the end of the letter a

parts.note: a crop is what is gathered in at harvest

indicators.note: reversing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: A harvest stored in a tower, turned round onto a stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns SILO into OLIS; CROP and OLIS go onto A.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified citadel of an ancient Greek city.
